draft.title: Reliable sources of geographical data
card: Geographers use data from many places, such as websites, reports and maps. Not every source can be trusted, so they check how reliable each one is.
Recent
the data is up to date. Old data may no longer describe a place that has changed.
Expert or official
it comes from a body that collects data as its job, such as a government agency, a university or a scientific organisation.
Evidence and no bias
it shows how the data was gathered and uses facts, not opinion. It does not leave out or twist facts to push one side.
draft.remember: A reliable source is recent, expert, backed by evidence and free of bias. Compare sources to test it.

a.q: Which source of data on river water quality is most reliable?
opts: A recent report by a state water authority, with its methods
A blog post by a local fan of the river, with no sources
An old pamphlet from a company that uses the river
A social media post by a person who visited once
a.why: The water authority is an official body, the report is recent, and it shows how the data was collected. The company pamphlet is tempting because it has data, but it is old and may be biased towards the company's interests.
a.clue: Look for the source that is recent, official and shows its evidence.

b.q: Priya is researching rainfall in a town in north-west Victoria. Two sources disagree. Which step best helps her decide which one to trust?
opts: Compare who made each source, when, and its methods
Choose the source with the longest, most detailed text
Choose the source that most people have shared online
Choose the source that agrees with her own opinion
b.why: Comparing the author, date and method shows which source is recent, expert and backed by evidence. Length and popularity can be tempting, but a long or widely shared source can still be old or biased.
b.clue: Think about the features of a reliable source, not how a source looks.

proposal.title: Reliable sources of geographical data
card: Recent
the data is up to date. Old data may no longer describe a place that has changed.
Expert or official
it comes from a body that collects data as its job, such as a government agency, a university or a scientific organisation.
Evidence and no bias
it shows how the data was gathered and uses facts, not opinion. It does not leave out or twist facts to push one side.
Comparing sources

checking data against other sources. If several reliable sources agree, the data is more likely to be trusted. If they disagree, check the author, date and method of each to see which meets the tests above.
proposal.remember: A reliable source is recent, expert, backed by evidence and free of bias. Checking it against other sources adds confidence.
